title: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon and CO(2─1) Emission at 50─150 pc Scales in 70 Nearby Galaxies
question: Characterize the relationship, scaling relations, environmental variations, and galaxy-to-galaxy scatter between CO(2-1) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission at 50-150 pc scales in 70 nearby star-forming galaxies.

data.sensitivity: approx +- 1 K km s^-1 in flat CO maps

what.value: PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) observations and strict masks

evidence.quote: We use PHANGS–ALMA CO (2-1) observations, which are described in (cite: leroy2021).
We additionally ensure that all significant CO emission is included by combining the fixed-width velocity mask with the “strict” mask from (cite: leroy2021).
We correct all intensities to face-on values by scaling by $\cos i$, where $i$ is the galaxy inclination from (cite: lang2020) and/or (cite: leroy2021).

what.value: Galaxy stellar masses and star formation rates

evidence.loc: Appendix: Cycle 2 JWST Imaging of PHANGS Galaxies
evidence.quote: lists the targets of both the Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 PHANGS Treasury, along with the list of bands observed and the stellar mass and SFR for each target

We also report the stellar mass and SFR/$M_\star$, adopted from (cite: leroy2019), the brightness of band $X$ in that galaxy at $I_{\rm \nu}^X = 1$ MJy sr$^{-1}$, the number of sight lines analyzed, and Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient relating the PAH and CO emission for each sightline.

what.value: Galaxy center masks based on near-IR stellar morphology

evidence.quote: We define galaxy centers using the masks in (cite: querejeta2021), which are based on near-IR stellar morphology, and nebular regions following (cite: santoro2022; groves2023), which are based on ionized gas emission observed by the VLT/MUSE as part of the PHANGS-MUSE survey (cite: emsellem2022).

what.value: Nebular / H II region masks from PHANGS-MUSE

evidence.quote: We define galaxy centers using the masks in (cite: querejeta2021), which are based on near-IR stellar morphology, and nebular regions following (cite: santoro2022; groves2023), which are based on ionized gas emission observed by the VLT/MUSE as part of the PHANGS-MUSE survey (cite: emsellem2022).
We use JWST MIRI and NIRCam imaging of 19 galaxies from the PHANGS-JWST Cycle 1 Treasury (cite: lee2023).

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST imaging and subtract stellar continuum to isolate PAH emission
recipe.method: Reduce Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 JWST NIRCam and MIRI mosaics using pjpipe, mask bright stars and background galaxies with elliptical apertures, and subtract stellar continuum from F770W (using 0.13*F200W or 0.22*F300M) and F335M (using F300M and F360M).
assumptions: Hot dust continuum in F770W and stellar continuum in F1130W are negligible and not subtracted

recipe.goal: Construct flat integrated ALMA CO(2-1) intensity maps
recipe.method: Integrate PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) cubes over a fixed-width velocity window (20-200 km/s) around the local mean velocity combined with the strict mask to capture >90% of CO flux without S/N clipping bias.
assumptions: No CO-to-H2 conversion factor is adopted when analyzing intensities

recipe.goal: Match angular resolution, reproject to common grid, correct for inclination, and apply environment and surface brightness masks
recipe.method: Convolve JWST images to CO(2-1) resolution using webbpsf PSFs, reproject CO, JWST, and environment masks onto a grid with pixel size 1/3 of CO PSF FWHM, multiply intensities by cos(i), and select bright pixels (I_F770W^PAH >= 0.5 MJy sr^-1; I_F335M^PAH > 0.1 MJy sr^-1).
key_parameters: Grid pixel size = 1/3 * CO PSF FWHM
assumptions: Regions with inclination-corrected I_F770W^PAH >= 0.5 MJy sr^-1 are dominated by molecular gas (Sigma_mol >= 4 M_sun pc^-2)

recipe.goal: Compute CO-to-PAH ratios, correlation coefficients, and power-law scaling relations across environments and individual galaxies
recipe.method: Compute Spearman rank correlation coefficients, median and MAD scatter of log10(CO/X), bin I_CO(2-1) in logarithmically-spaced bins of MIR intensity I_X, and fit power-law relations using linmix for the full sample, sub-environments, and individual galaxies, as well as fitting galaxy normalizations against M_star and SFR/M_star.

answer_key.quantity: Power-law slope m for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (all pixels)

evidence.quote: $m=0.90\pm 0.07$, agree reasonably well with previous work on much smaller samples or at lower resolution

answer_key.quantity: Power-law intercept b for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (all pixels, at x_0 = 1.44)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient r for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (all pixels)
Power-law slope m for CO(2-1) vs F335M_PAH (all pixels)
Power-law slope m for CO(2-1) vs F1130W (all pixels)
Power-law slope m for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (outside centers)
Power-law slope m for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (galaxy centers)
Median log10(CO(2-1) / F770W_PAH) ratio (nebular regions, Cycle 1)
Median log10(CO(2-1) / F770W_PAH) ratio (diffuse regions, Cycle 1)

evidence.quote: Specifically, the normalization of the CO-PAH relation scatters by $\pm 0.17$ dex from galaxy to galaxy.

answer_key.quantity: Renormalized power-law slope m for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (all pixels)
Renormalized power-law intercept b for CO(2-1) vs F770W_PAH (all pixels, at x_0 = 1.44)

not_stated_but_needed: Exact velocity integration window widths and reference velocity tracer chosen for each individual galaxy's flat CO(2-1) map
Exact F335M continuum subtraction equations/coefficients from H. Koziol et al. (in preparation)
Coordinates and dimensions of the elliptical apertures used to mask bright foreground stars and background galaxies
Exact bin widths and spacing used for the logarithmically-spaced MIR intensity bins prior to linmix fitting
SpecificPHANGS-ALMA internal/public data release version used
missing_for_reproduction: Exact F335M continuum subtraction coefficients/recipe from Koziol et al. (in preparation)
Exact background anchoring procedures for Cycle 2 JWST images from Koziol et al. (in preparation) and Pathak et al. (in preparation)
Exact per-galaxy velocity window widths and reference velocity fields used to generate the flat CO(2-1) maps
Locations and sizes of manual elliptical masks for bright foreground stars and background galaxies
Exact number or width of logarithmic bins used before linmix regression
score_reason: The statistical analysis, pixel gridding, thresholds, and fitting methods (linmix, webbpsf, pjpipe) are clearly described and high-level PHANGS-ALMA and PHANGS-JWST products are publicly archived, but several preprocessing details (flat CO map velocity windows, F335M continuum subtraction coefficients from in-prep work, star masks, and exact bin widths) are not explicitly stated in the paper.
rediscovery_reason: The main findings are clean numerical power-law scaling relations and correlation coefficients across 70 galaxies using public PHANGS-ALMA and PHANGS-JWST treasury datasets, making it well-suited for reproducing the CO-PAH scaling relations from processed maps.
